transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-02-12 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Luis Gomez (Redwood SE), Ava Martinez (Acme Infra), Ben Walker (Acme Sec), Caroline Li (Acme PM)

Auto-generated summary (brief):
- Discovery for Private / VPC deployment. Primary concerns: network topology, VPC peering vs PrivateLink, cross-account peering, region constraints (eu-west-1), IP planning, KMS/encryption, audit logs and SOC2.
- Customer wants pilot in eu-west-1 with private endpoints and strict egress controls. Timeline: pilot decision in 3 weeks.
- Next steps agreed: Redwood to share architecture doc, peering checklist, and schedule deep technical dive.

Topics: networking, VPC peering, PrivateLink, Transit Gateway, IP ranges, KMS, SOC2, audit logs, timeline, pilot sizing

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining, I think we have about 45 to 55 minutes - happy to run through high level and then dive into the networking questions. you good with that?
[00:18] Ava: yeah, sounds good. thanks, Jordan. appreciate you guys setting this up. Ben's on for security, caroline for product, i'm on infra.
[00:29] Jordan: awesome. quick intros, maya and luis are our SEs who handle private deployments and network setups.
[00:34] Maya: hey all, hi.
[00:36] Luis: hi.
[00:38] Ben: hi.
[00:40] Jordan: cool. caroline, can you give us a bit of context on why you're evaluating Redwood Private?
[00:48] Caroline: sure - our main requirement is no egress of patient PII outside our VPC, also we need control over KMS keys and we have data residency must be in ireland eu-west-1. we're evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private, but private looks like the best fit given HIPAA-ish constraints and our internal policies.
[01:05] Jordan: makes sense. ava, can you say what your current infra looks like?
[01:10] Ava: we're on AWS, accounts in a few org units, primary workloads run in eu-west-1, we use EKS, and we have a Transit Gateway between prod and analytics. our security posture prohibits internet-facing endpoints for internal model traffic. so private endpoints or peering is required.
[01:26] Maya: ok, that's helpful. quick question — do you want Redwood hosted but with private connectivity (PrivateLink) or a full Private deployment (control plane in your VPC / on-prem)?
[01:38] Ben: ideally control plane in our VPC, so we manage the network and keys. but we'll consider private endpoints if full private is heavier. cost and ops overhead are factors.
[01:47] Jordan: got it. maybe we can talk through both. for hosted with PrivateLink we provide service endpoints that sit in your VPC via AWS PrivateLink, not crossing the public internet; for Private deployment we can install the control plane into your VPC and integrate with your KMS and SSO. each has tradeoffs on ops responsibility.
[02:05] [small crosstalk]
[02:08] Ava: can you clarify about IP ranges? we need to plan CIDRs.
[02:12] Luis: yes, so for PrivateLink option you typically need to allocate some elastic network interfaces and we ask for a /28 or /27 depending on scale. for full Private deployment we need a set of IPs for agents and the control plane; that is larger — we usually work from a dedicated management VPC and peer it to app VPCs via Transit Gateway or peering.
[02:33] Ben: Transit Gateway is likely our preference given multiple accounts. how does cross-account peering work with your deployments? any gotchas?
[02:41] Maya: it's straightforward — we either peer the Redwood-managed VPC into your org account using cross-account peering, or we deploy the Redwood control plane inside your account so there's no cross-account routing. if you use Transit Gateway we can attach our deployment VPC as an attachment and route accordingly. note: TGW attachment requires route planning and potentially NAT for outbound model downloads.
[03:01] Jordan: also worth flagging that some customers prefer PrivateLink because it avoids peering and route table complexity, but it can complicate service discovery for multi-account setups.
[03:12] Caroline: what's the impact on latency if we go through PrivateLink vs peering vs in-account deployment?
[03:18] Luis: in-account deployment is lowest latency, peering/TGW is slightly higher but still sub-10ms intra-region typically, PrivateLink adds a small proxy hop — depends on AZ and ELB. for eu-west-1 we usually see 5-15ms differences in our tests.
[03:33] Ava: we will also need specific egress controls — e.g. only allow outbound to S3 for model downloads, and everything else blocked. how do you support limited egress?
[03:43] Maya: we can set up NAT rules that allow only specific S3 endpoints and our artifact storage. for hosted PrivateLink we host artifacts in a signed S3 bucket and we can provide VPC endpoints to it. for Private deployment you host artifacts on your side and the agents pull from your S3 with IAM roles.
[03:59] Ben: KMS — we must manage the keys. can Redwood integrate with our KMS?
[04:05] Maya: yes, in Private deployment we integrate with customer-managed KMS/HSM for model encryption at rest, and we emit audit logs to your CloudWatch or S3. for hosted PrivateLink we have a limited model where keys remain with Redwood, but we can discuss bring-your-own-key for some contracts.
[04:21] Ben: ok. SOC2 and compliance — do you have the reports?
[04:25] Jordan: yes, we have SOC2 Type II and ISO docs; i'll share a link after the call. also we have a customer audit pack.
[04:33] Caroline: timeline — we want to pilot in 3 weeks if possible. is that realistic?
[04:39] Luis: for a simple PrivateLink connection, yes — 2-3 weeks is doable: IP planning, security review, and a short config. for full Private deployment in-account it may be 4-8 weeks depending on change controls and approvals.
[04:53] Ava: do you support region constraints? we need eu-west-1 only.
[04:58] Maya: yes — we can deploy in eu-west-1. one note: some open models have larger binaries which may require GPU types that are not uniform across regions; we'll surface model+runtime recommendations for eu-west-1.
[05:12] Jordan: can you share your current model workloads? token volumes, typical sequences?
[05:17] Caroline: for pilot it's small: 2k qps equivalent over peak day? well, it's actually more like 200 qps, but we want headroom. average prompt lengths 150 tokens.
[05:29] Maya: ok that's small and likely fits on a few GPUs or in a small dedicated cluster. we'll recommend config.
[05:34] [pause]
[05:36] Ava: two more network questions: do you support VPC peering with overlapping CIDRs? we have some legacy ranges.
[05:44] Luis: overlapping CIDRs are tricky — peering won't work with overlap. options: use Transit Gateway with NAT translation, use PrivateLink, or renumber the VPC. we can help with a plan but renumbering is often heavy.
[05:58] Ben: interesting. and about private endpoints — will we be able to authenticate using SAML/SSO and RBAC integrated with our IDP?
[06:06] Maya: yes, for Private deployment we integrate with SAML/SSO and can map roles to RBAC. we can also push logs to your SIEM. for hosted PrivateLink we support OIDC/SAML for control plane access but the options for full RBAC mapping vary by deployment.
[06:20] Jordan: any blockers on IP ranges or security policies from your side, Ava?
[06:24] Ava: our infra team requires a list of IPs / subnets and account IDs for WHITELISTing. we'll also need a diagram and a runbook for failover.
[06:33] Luis: we'll deliver an IP checklist + runbooks. we'll also provide our recommended CIDR ranges to avoid collisions.
[06:39] [15-minute mark check-in]
[15:12] Jordan: quick pivot — Caroline asked about billing and committed capacity. how are you thinking about cost?
[15:20] Caroline: we have a limited budget — we want committed capacity if it reduces unit cost but don't want long multi-year lock-ins for pilot.
[15:29] Jordan: we can offer a short-term reserved pilot, or metered usage with a commitment discount. i'll send sample pricing scenarios.
[15:36] Ava: one security nuance — all debug logs must remain in our account. do you support log redaction or do you push raw logs to our S3?
[15:45] Maya: in Private deployment we push logs to your S3/CloudWatch; you control retention and access. for hosted modes we can stream logs to customer buckets for enterprise plans.
[15:55] Ben: what about inference caching and KV cache? does that store any PII?
[16:00] Luis: by default we treat caches as ephemeral and do not persist PII, but configuration matters. in Private deployment you control cache retention and where it's stored; we can disable prefix caching for PII-heavy prompts.
[16:13] [brief silence]
[16:20] Caroline: sounds good. what do you need from us to start the pilot?
[16:24] Jordan: three things: AWS account IDs and VPC CIDRs you want to connect, a short security questionnaire answered, and a contact for IAM roles and KMS.
[16:33] Ava: i'll send the CIDRs and account ids.
[16:35] Ben: i'll review the security questionnaire.
[16:37] Jordan: perfect. we'll assemble a pilot SOW and architecture options: PrivateLink path vs Private in-account.
[16:45] Maya: also to note for eu-west-1 — if you plan to run larger models we'll recommend specific instance families; we'll include that in the doc.
[16:55] Caroline: any other risks or typical hiccups?
[17:00] Luis: approvals and IP planning are the biggest; org policy for deploying third-party control planes in-account can add time. sometimes audit teams request extra encryption attestations.
[17:10] Jordan: okay should we recap next steps?
[17:13] Caroline: yes please.
[17:15] Jordan: recap: Redwood to share Private deployment architecture doc and PrivateLink checklist, schedule deep technical dive with infra and security (Maya + Luis), provide pricing scenarios, and share SOC2/KMS docs. Acme to share account IDs, CIDRs, and security contact.
[17:31] Ava: correct. we'll aim to get the account ids and CIDRs by Feb 14.
[17:36] Ben: i'll review and follow up on the questionnaire.
[17:40] Jordan: great. i'll send meeting notes and the links. thanks all.
[17:45] Caroline: thanks everyone.
[17:48] [call ends]
